key_insight: Using a reverse-predictivity analysis, the authors show that only a subset of units within artificial neural networks reliably align with primate brain responses, revealing a substantial misalignment between ANNs and brains despite strong bidirectional alignment observed between two primate brains.
problem_solved: Clarifies whether and how neural network units truly correspond to biological neural responses by introducing a bidirectional comparison that exposes asymmetries missed by standard forward-only predictivity measures.
method: Define and compute reverse predictivity (predicting ANN unit activity from primate brain responses) alongside conventional forward predictivity.
Compare bidirectional predictivity between ANNs and primate brains and between two primate brains to quantify alignment and bidirectionality.
Identify and characterize the subset of ANN units that show reliable alignment with brain responses and measure the overall misalignment.
impact: Highlights that many ANN units do not map cleanly to brain activity, prompting AI/ML practitioners to use bidirectional metrics for model evaluation, focus on aligned subpopulations for interpretability, and guide design of more brain-like architectures.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram with bidirectional arrows between a brain icon and an ANN diagram showing thicker arrow for brain→brain and thinner for brain↔ANN
Bar chart or stacked bars showing proportion of ANN units classified as aligned vs misaligned
Heatmap of predictivity scores across ANN layers and units to reveal localized pockets of alignment
Scatter plot comparing forward vs reverse predictivity for units (quadrant highlights aligned subset)
paper_title: Reverse predictivity for bidirectional comparison of neural networks and biological brains
